newsitem.title: CHINA: China sobers up drunken panda sperm.
newsitem.headline: China sobers up drunken panda sperm.

text.p: Chinese scientists have discovered a way to bring new vim and vigour to panda sperm used to artificially inseminate females of the low libido species, the China Daily said on Thursday.

A new thawing and culture solution had boosted pregnancies by keeping sperm alive for up to 21 hours outside the panda's body, it quoted Professor Chen Dayuan of the Institute of Zoology of the Chinese Academy of Sciences as saying. "In the past, the old solution had made most of the sperm 'drunk' and lose their mobility upon entering the female panda," Chen said.
The newer blend had helped to produce 24 panda cubs between 1990 and 1995, China Daily quoted Chen's team as reporting in a recent scientific journal.

The official Xinhua news agency on Wednesday said China's panda fertility researchers had found that hormone supplements could cause sexual excitement among female pandas that normally looked on males with little more than contempt.
Only 10 percent of giant pandas could mate naturally and their lack of fecundity was the main reason for their endangered status, Xinhua said.
